Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.domain.user

Interface UserRepository

All Known Implementing Classes:
UserRepositoryAdapter
public interface UserRepository
Domain repository port for the User aggregate.

Pure Java — no Spring annotations. The adapter implementing this interface lives in infrastructure/persistence/adapter/ and bridges to Spring Data JPA.

The original surface (EPIC-03) covered the read/write paths login and self password change need. EPIC-05 / US-05-001 extends it with the admin-side read/write paths: the duplicate-email guard, the keyset-paged list, and hard-delete. Hard-delete cascade through agents → conversations → messages is provided by the V001 FK chain (REQ-USR-006) and is verified by the EPIC-02 cascade contract test; the port contract here is "the row is gone after delete(UserId) returns".

    • existsByEmail

      boolean existsByEmail(Email email)
      Returns true iff a user with the given email exists. Callers pass the canonicalized (lowercase) value via Email#value() — the lower(email) functional unique index (V004) keeps the lookup O(1). Used by CreateUserService (US-05-004) for the duplicate-email pre-flight check; the value-object encapsulation is what makes "supply the canonical value" a non-issue here.

    • listAll

      Page<User> listAll(Cursor cursor, int pageSize)
      Returns one page of users ordered newest-first ((createdAt, id) DESC). Pass cursor = null for the first page. pageSize is the maximum number of items in the returned page; the adapter is responsible for detecting the presence of a next page and emitting a non-null Page.nextCursor() accordingly. Used by ListUsersService (US-05-005).

    • delete

      void delete(UserId id)
      Hard-deletes the user identified by id. The FK cascade chain in V001 is responsible for removing every owned agent, conversation, and message (REQ-USR-006); the integration test in US-05-008 verifies this through the REST surface. A non-existent id is a silent no-op at this layer — the use case (US-05-008) is responsible for the 404 by reading the row first.
